input: Set up a side hustle tracking spreadsheet

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The spreadsheet structure changes completely depending on whether it tracks income/expenses, time spent, client work, product sales, or all of the above.
A solo freelancer needs different columns and views than someone managing a side hustle with a partner or team.
The type of side hustle (e.g. freelancing, e-commerce, content creation, tutoring) dictates which specific metrics and categories are most relevant.
Whether the user wants a quick-start template or a fully custom build affects how much time and effort goes into setup.
The choice of tool (Google Sheets, Excel, Notion, Airtable) determines the features available and the format of the final deliverable.
Some users want a simple flat log; others want dashboards, charts, and automated summaries — knowing this shapes the design heavily.
Knowing the single most important thing the user wants to get out of the spreadsheet (e.g. see monthly profit, prepare for taxes, spot growth trends) ensures the design prioritises the right output.

gold.taskTitle: Build a side hustle tracking spreadsheet
gold.taskDescription: Create a spreadsheet to track the performance, finances, or activity of one or more side hustles.

questions.title: What specifically do you want to track in it?
questions.description: Clarify whether the spreadsheet should cover income, expenses, time, client projects, sales, or a combination — this determines the core columns and structure.

questions.title: What kind of side hustle is this for?
questions.description: Identify the nature of the hustle (freelancing, e-commerce, content creation, tutoring, etc.) so the categories and metrics used are specific and relevant.

questions.title: Are you running this alone or with someone else?
questions.description: Determine if the spreadsheet needs to accommodate multiple contributors, split income/expenses, or shared visibility.

questions.title: Which tool do you want to build this in?
questions.description: Establish whether the user prefers Google Sheets, Excel, Notion, Airtable, or another platform, as this affects formulas, automation, and sharing options.

questions.title: How much time can you spend setting this up?
questions.description: Understand if the user needs a quick, minimal template they can use today or is willing to invest time in a more robust, custom-built system.

questions.title: Do you want a simple log or visual dashboards and summaries?
questions.description: Determine the desired level of complexity — a plain data-entry log vs. automated totals, charts, and a summary dashboard.

questions.title: What is the one key thing this spreadsheet must show you?
questions.description: Identify the primary output the user cares most about — e.g. monthly net profit, tax-ready expense records, or growth over time — so the design is built around that goal.
